title: powder-doser: design files, firmware, test data, design log, and AI interaction history for an open-source auger powder doser
description:
Design files, firmware, test data, design log, and AI prompt and response records for an open-source, 3D-printed, single-channel auger powder doser built from printed parts and off-the-shelf electronics for under $200 (plus an analytical balance). A $6 microcontroller turns, tilts, and taps a printed auger until the balance reads the requested mass. The mechanical parts were first designed with generative AI (LLM coding agents writing CAD code, and a chat-driven CAD tool) under human direction, and later redrawn in Fusion 360.

The release contains the parametric CAD source (CadQuery, OpenSCAD, KCL), STEP and STL exports, the MicroPython firmware, KiCad schematics, the raw test-protocol records and per-dose record for 13 powders, the analysis and figure scripts, the design log, and the AI prompt and response logs. It accompanies the article "An open-source, 3D-printed auger powder doser designed with generative artificial intelligence" (Digital Discovery, submitted).
